text.arabic_uthmani: أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَٰكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ فَأَرَدتُّ أَنْ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٌۭ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًۭا

words.gloss_range: tafṣīl particle that opens the first itemized explanation and requires a following fa-response

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the required response particle after the opening tafṣīl frame

words.prose: {{ar:أَمَّا}} ({{tr:ammā}}) shifts the narration into ordered explanation: the ship becomes the first case in the promised disclosure from 18:78, and the particle expects the response carried by the next {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}). It also opens the triptych continued by the matched explanations at 18:80 and 18:82, so this first word controls the ayah’s discourse mode before any rationale appears.

topics.headline: tafṣīl opening organizes the explanation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse has shifted from event narration into ordered case-by-case explanation.
topics.reason: The particle is grammatically the tafṣīl launcher and requires a response fa, so the ship is introduced as the first explained case.

topics.headline: first panel of the promised triptych
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the explanation promised in 18:78 begins here as the first panel and will continue with matching panels at 18:80 and 18:82.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give the 18:79, 18:80, and 18:82 sequence and the boundary from the prior promise, with no guardrail contradiction.

words.gloss_range: the known, definite ship from the earlier incident, now made the topic of explanation
words.root_gloss_range: vessel/carrier field with supplied scraping and surface-treatment associations; locally the maritime vessel sense is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the later indefinite ship noun under universal scope

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّفِينَةُ}} ({{tr:al-safīnatu}}) names the known vessel from 18:71 as the explicit topic, with definiteness, nominative position, and feminine agreement making it the object now under explanation. The supplied {{ar:س ف ن}} ({{tr:s-f-n}}) surface/scraping field keeps the vessel materially vivid, but the sea-work context selects an actual maritime ship, and the rare lexeme will return near the close as generic {{ar:سَفِينَةٍ}} ({{tr:safīnatin}}).

topics.headline: known ship becomes the explicit topic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object questioned in 18:71 is now the named, definite topic whose status must be explained.
topics.reason: Definiteness, nominative topic position, and feminine agreement with the following verb all point back to the known ship.

topics.headline: scraping surface image remains local color
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ship as a worked surface-carrier whose controlled marking matters, while the local sense remains an actual maritime vessel.
topics.reason: The supplied root image supports surface salience, but the sea phrase selects the concrete watercraft sense rather than a broad carrier abstraction.

topics.headline: rare ship lexeme anchors the episode
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a rare vessel word recurring from 18:71 into 18:79 and then toward the generic ship threat later in the ayah.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows tie the word to 18:71 and to the later same-ayah ship noun, making the recurrence structurally useful.

words.gloss_range: apodotic fa answering the opening tafṣīl particle and moving the topic into its status clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the opening tafṣīl particle that requires this response fa
the topicalized ship answered by this fa
the status verb introduced by the apodotic fa

words.prose: This {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the required response hinge after {{ar:أَمَّا}} ({{tr:ammā}}), not a loose chronological connector. It moves the topic {{ar:ٱلسَّفِينَةُ}} ({{tr:al-safīnatu}}) into the status clause {{ar:كَانَتْ}} ({{tr:kānat}}), while the later {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) at word 10 will perform a different causal turn.

topics.headline: required fa completes the topic frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first fa is not a loose “then”; it is the hinge that makes the tafṣīl topic into a complete explanation.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify this fa as the response marker after the opening tafṣīl particle, distinct from the later causal fa.

words.gloss_range: feminine perfect being-verb used with possessive li- to report established ownership
words.root_gloss_range: being, existence, state, formation, and place-of-being; locally possession-status is selected by the li- predicate

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the later masculine existential being-verb in the threat clause

words.prose: {{ar:كَانَتْ}} ({{tr:kānat}}) reports an already-established status: the ship belonged to poor owners before the protective damage occurred. Its feminine ending keeps the ship as grammatical subject, and the later masculine {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) echoes the same being-root with a different function, moving from vulnerable possession to threatening existence.

topics.headline: being-verb states prior ownership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ship already belonged to vulnerable owners before the intervention, so the damage answers a prior property relation.
topics.reason: The perfect verb plus possessive li-predicate reports an established ownership status rather than creating a new state.

topics.headline: feminine form keeps the ship as subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar keeps the ship, not the owners, as the subject whose status is being explained.
topics.reason: The feminine ending agrees with the feminine ship topic and routes the predicate back to it.

topics.headline: two being-clauses contrast possession and threat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the later echo: one being-clause secures poor ownership, while another introduces the king’s threatening existence.
topics.reason: The same root recurs locally in different functions, and the rows connect this pattern with the explanatory sequence.

words.gloss_range: possessive preposition fused to the owner noun, selecting ownership rather than mere benefit

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the being-verb whose predicate is the possessive li- phrase

words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) makes the poor people owners of the ship, not merely beneficiaries of it. The particle’s broader range is context-governed: here the {{ar:كَانَتْ}} ({{tr:kānat}}) construction selects possession, unlike adverse uses elsewhere in the surah.

topics.headline: li marks poor people as owners
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the poor are proprietors of the ship, not merely beneficiaries or bystanders.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the owner noun as the possessive predicate of the being-clause.

topics.headline: same particle takes opposite local valences
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this particle’s local value must be read from its construction: here ownership, not the adverse allotment seen elsewhere in the surah.
topics.reason: The cross-surah contrast is useful as a range check, but local syntax selects possession.

words.gloss_range: indefinite broken plural for destitute owners, immediately characterized as sea-workers
words.root_gloss_range: stillness, dwelling, repose, and poverty-as-constrained condition; locally the poor-owner sense is active
words.prose: {{ar:مَسَٰكِينَ}} ({{tr:masākīna}}) identifies the owners as socially vulnerable yet immediately active: the following plural work-clause makes them laboring people, not an abstract poverty category. The {{ar:س ك ن}} ({{tr:s-k-n}}) stillness/rest field becomes pointed by contrast, because those marked by poverty-as-constriction survive through motion and risk in the sea. Its intensive pattern, major distribution, and geminated variant make that vulnerability feel severe and pressed, while the canonical local reading remains poor working owners.

topics.headline: destitute owners remain active workers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the owners are both economically vulnerable and active agents whose livelihood depends on the ship.
topics.reason: Case, pronoun routing, and the attached work clause make the poor people owners and workers, not an abstract poverty label.

topics.headline: poverty stillness is inverted by sea labor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that people marked by the stillness/rest field are shown surviving through motion and risk at sea.
topics.reason: The root field can color the poverty term, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as poor owners.

topics.headline: intensive poverty form and variant pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word is a pressure point for severe vulnerability, with variant and distribution evidence intensifying but not replacing the standard poor-owner reading.
topics.reason: The supplied variant and intensive-pattern rows support heightened vulnerability, but the canonical local form remains the base reading.

words.gloss_range: indicative imperfect plural naming ongoing work without a direct object in a sea-locative frame
words.root_gloss_range: doing, working, acting, and deed-accountability; locally sustained livelihood labor is selected
words.prose: {{ar:يَعْمَلُونَ}} ({{tr:yaʿmalūna}}) presents their labor as ongoing livelihood, with the poor owners recovered as the plural subject and no direct object distracting from the activity itself. The form excludes employ/use branches and lets ordinary sea labor join the surah’s wider {{ar:ع م ل}} ({{tr:ʿ-m-l}}) concern with consequential work, including 18:110.

topics.headline: imperfect verb names habitual work
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ship supports ongoing livelihood, not a single completed errand.
topics.reason: The indicative imperfect with no direct object and a locative frame presents sustained labor by the poor owners.

topics.headline: direct work excludes employ/use branches
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the owners themselves work; the form does not cast them as being employed, appointed, or used by someone else.
topics.reason: The local Form I imperfect selects direct working rather than causative or Form X employ/use branches.

topics.headline: labor joins the surah’s work vocabulary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that ordinary maritime labor participates in the surah’s wider concern with consequential work and deeds.
topics.reason: The rows connect local livelihood labor with neighboring roots and same-surah work/deed recurrences.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition that makes the sea the domain of the owners’ work

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the work verb whose domain is supplied by this preposition

words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) makes the sea the domain in which the owners work, so the environment is part of the livelihood description rather than scenery. Its in/on range leaves surface navigation and sea labor productive while keeping the phrase tightly attached to {{ar:يَعْمَلُونَ}} ({{tr:yaʿmalūna}}).

topics.headline: fī makes the sea the work-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sea is not a backdrop; it is the medium inside which the owners’ livelihood happens.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the sea noun and attaches the location to the work clause, with productive in/on domain range.

words.gloss_range: definite singular sea as the concrete work-domain of the poor owners
words.root_gloss_range: sea, broad water, expanse, and supplied cutting/opening associations; locally the navigable sea-domain is selected
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْبَحْرِ}} ({{tr:al-baḥri}}) completes the maritime livelihood scene: a definite sea is where the poor owners work and why the ship is necessary. The broader {{ar:ب ح ر}} ({{tr:b-ḥ-r}}) expanse and cutting/opening field can color the later flaw, while the same sea thread narrows the journey setting of 18:60 and 18:63 into a workplace before expanding again in 18:109.

topics.headline: definite sea completes the labor scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a coherent maritime livelihood scene: ship, poor workers, sea, and later ship-threat all belong together.
topics.reason: The definite genitive noun is the governed work-domain and mediates the ship-work-threat sequence.

topics.headline: sea expanse and cutting imagery color the flaw
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sea’s vast/cutting field sharpens why a surface breach or mark on a vessel matters, while the word still means the concrete sea.
topics.reason: The supplied root field supports cutting/opening color, but local syntax selects the noun for the sea-domain.

topics.headline: sea narrows from journey motif to workplace
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sea of the journey becomes the concrete workplace in 18:79, before later expanding again into the knowledge image at 18:109.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply concrete same-surah references at 18:60, 18:63, 18:79, and 18:109.

words.gloss_range: causal-sequential fa linking the owners’ situation to the servant’s intervention
words.prose: The second {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the owners’ vulnerable status and sea-work into the reason for intervention. Unlike the apodotic {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) at word 3, this one carries the explanation from circumstance into deliberate protective intent.

topics.headline: second fa turns circumstance into intervention
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the logical turn from poor owners’ situation to the servant’s chosen protective action.
topics.reason: The second fa differs from the apodotic fa and links the established vulnerability to the intention clause.

words.gloss_range: perfect first-person Form IV intention, with the flawing clause as its content
words.root_gloss_range: willing, intending, seeking, and related turning/manipulation branches; locally directed intention is selected
words.prose: {{ar:أَرَدتُّ}} ({{tr:aradtu}}) makes the servant’s agency explicit: he claims a completed first-person intention, and the following clause supplies the intended content. The Form IV will is directed rather than wandering or manipulative, and it begins an agency gradient later contrasted with the Lord’s intention at 18:82.

topics.headline: servant claims personal intention
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker accepts agency for the ship incident instead of leaving it as anonymous fate.
topics.reason: The perfect first-person suffix supplies the speaker as agent and states completed volition.

topics.headline: will governs the flawing clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the defect was the content of a plan, not an accidental side effect.
topics.reason: The intention verb governs the following complement clause, making the flawing the intended object.

topics.headline: intention root calibrates human and divine agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this “I intended” begins an agency gradient later contrasted with the Lord’s intention in 18:82.
topics.reason: The Form IV reading is locally directed will; broader seeking or seduction branches are useful range checks but not active senses here.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive complementizer that turns the following act into the object of intention

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the intention verb that governs this complementizer
the subjunctive flawing verb governed by this complementizer

words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) binds will to action by making {{ar:أَعِيبَهَا}} ({{tr:aʿībahā}}) the subjunctive complement of {{ar:أَرَدتُّ}} ({{tr:aradtu}}). The damaging act is therefore grammatically inside intention, not a separate report standing on its own.

topics.headline: an turns will into intended action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the damaging act remains grammatically inside the intention, not as an independent assertion.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following subjunctive and converts the action clause into the object of the intention verb.

words.gloss_range: Form IV subjunctive with object suffix: to cause a defect in the known ship
words.root_gloss_range: fault, blemish, defect, and legal or practical unsoundness; locally controlled defect-making is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the final coercive manner word contrasted with the protective defect

words.prose: {{ar:أَعِيبَهَا}} ({{tr:aʿībahā}}) reframes the earlier puncture from 18:71 as deliberate defect-making on the same known ship. The negative defect becomes protective because the royal policy targets serviceable vessels; the unique {{ar:ع ي ب}} ({{tr:ʿ-y-b}}) form stands opposite final {{ar:غَصْبًا}} ({{tr:ghaṣban}}), distinguishing limited impairment from coercive seizure.

topics.headline: causative defect targets the known ship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act is deliberate defect-making on the same known ship, not mere observation of damage.
topics.reason: The Form IV subjunctive with suffix object marks caused defect under the intention clause.

topics.headline: defect protects against sound-ship seizure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ethical reversal: a negative defect becomes protective because the king targets serviceable ships.
topics.reason: The defect range includes practical/legal unsoundness, and the variant evidence around sound/intact ships explains the protective mechanism.

topics.headline: earlier puncture is reinterpreted as impairment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act described as puncturing in 18:71 is now reframed as deliberate limited impairment.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows supply the 18:71 contrast and the hapax Form IV profile, with no evidence blocking the reinterpretation.

topics.headline: unique defect echoes final usurpation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two rare force-words at opposite poles: limited protective impairment and final coercive usurpation.
topics.reason: The hapax and sound-texture rows support emphasis, while the local semantic contrast remains the main payoff.

words.gloss_range: wāw linking the intention clause to the background threat, either circumstantially or resumptively
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) introduces the king clause as the concealed background to the intention rather than as another simple step in sequence. Whether read circumstantially or resumptively, it pivots from the servant’s act to the hidden condition that made the act protective.

topics.headline: wa reveals the hidden condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the king clause arrives as the concealed background to the intention, not as a simple next event.
topics.reason: Both circumstantial and resumptive readings preserve the same local payoff: the threat clause explains the prior intention.

words.gloss_range: masculine perfect existential verb introducing the already-existing hidden threat
words.root_gloss_range: being and existence range; locally existential presence is selected rather than possession

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the earlier feminine possession verb contrasted with this existential verb

words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) states an existing threat: there was a king beyond the owners. Its masculine form and existential construction distinguish it from earlier {{ar:كَانَتْ}} ({{tr:kānat}}), so the repeated being-root frames both poor possession and royal danger.

topics.headline: existential kāna makes threat already present
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the king’s danger was an existing state of affairs, justifying preemptive defect-making.
topics.reason: The perfect existential construction with fronted adverb and delayed subject states an established hidden threat.

topics.headline: masculine form prepares the delayed king
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the syntax pass through the hidden location before naming the masculine agent.
topics.reason: The masculine form and word order distinguish this clause from the earlier feminine possession clause.

topics.headline: second being-clause contrasts with ownership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices one being-root frame for poor possession and another for threatening royal presence.
topics.reason: The rows connect the repeated root to local seizure, kingship, and the explanatory triptych.

words.gloss_range: spatial adverb with owner-facing suffix, marking a hidden beyond/ahead/behind horizon
words.root_gloss_range: concealment, beyondness, and what is hidden from view; locally spatial relation carries epistemic hiddenness

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: variant reading that fixes the direction as in front of them

words.prose: {{ar:وَرَآءَهُم}} ({{tr:warāʾahum}}) locates the threat beyond the owners’ horizon, with the suffix measuring danger relative to the poor workers themselves. The standard wording leaves behind/beyond/ahead productive, while the variant {{ar:أَمَامَهُمْ}} ({{tr:amāmahum}}) fixes the forward reading; either way the word performs the hidden-cause logic promised by the taʾwīl in 18:78, with 19:5 showing comparable beyondness for what lies after or beyond someone.

topics.headline: warāʾ keeps hidden direction productive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the threat is spatially and epistemically beyond the owners, with the standard wording allowing behind/beyond/ahead while the variant fixes the forward reading.
topics.reason: The standard addād range and the variant are valid evidence, but the canonical form remains directionally open rather than fixed only to “in front”.

topics.headline: suffix measures threat against the workers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the king is located relative to the poor workers’ route, not as a detached political fact.
topics.reason: The suffix points back to the poor working owners and fixes the spatial horizon around them.

topics.headline: beyondness performs the promised hidden explanation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the explanation crossing the horizon that Mūsā could not see: the hidden cause is named as beyond them, with 19:5 showing the same beyondness for what lies after or beyond a person.
topics.reason: The rows make hiddenness and beyondness the mechanism of the taʾwīl promised in 18:78, with 19:5 as a concrete comparison.

words.gloss_range: indefinite singular king as the delayed subject and agent of seizure
words.root_gloss_range: kingship, possession, dominion, ownership, and power; locally human sovereign power is selected
words.prose: {{ar:مَّلِكٌ}} ({{tr:malikun}}) arrives as an indefinite delayed subject, emerging from the hidden spatial phrase before being defined by what he takes. The {{ar:م ل ك}} ({{tr:m-l-k}}) power field sharpens the social opposition: poor owners hold the ship, but royal power threatens to override ownership by seizure. The same root belongs to a broader dominion vocabulary, but this local king is a negative human instance, and the indefinite ending links the anonymous agent with the final coercive manner.

topics.headline: indefinite king emerges from concealment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ruler is introduced not by name or realm but by a seizure practice.
topics.reason: The indefinite delayed subject controls the following verb, which describes the king through taking.

topics.headline: sovereign power threatens poor ownership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the social opposition between poor owners and royal power that can override ownership by force.
topics.reason: The root family links rule and ownership, while local context distinguishes legitimate possession from coercive sovereignty.

topics.headline: earthly king contrasts broader dominion field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this king as a morally negative instance within a broader dominion vocabulary, with the indefinite sound pattern binding agent and manner.
topics.reason: Cross-surah dominion echoes and cadence are useful as contrast, but local meaning is the human king who seizes.

words.gloss_range: indicative imperfect taking verb, defined by its universal object and coercive manner
words.root_gloss_range: taking, receiving, seizing, adopting, and holding accountable; locally seizure is selected by the final manner word

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the final manner word that narrows taking into coercive seizure

words.prose: {{ar:يَأْخُذُ}} ({{tr:yaʾkhudhu}}) makes the king’s practice ongoing and object-directed: he takes the whole ship class, not merely one vessel. The verb’s broad taking range is narrowed by final {{ar:غَصْبًا}} ({{tr:ghaṣban}}) into coercive confiscation, and the same-surah taking vocabulary includes illegitimate taking at 18:50.

topics.headline: imperfect taking defines a policy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the king’s action is systemic: he keeps taking ships, so one ship needs preemptive protection.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb with universal object functions as an adjectival clause defining the king’s ongoing practice.

topics.headline: final manner word sharpens taking into seizure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that broad “taking” is morally fixed as coercive confiscation only when the final manner word arrives.
topics.reason: The root has broader taking/adopting/accountability uses, but local coercive manner narrows the sense.

topics.headline: taking root joins local existence and sea-loss threads
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local seizure as part of a same-surah taking vocabulary, including illegitimate taking in 18:50.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete same-surah links, while the local clause remains physical ship seizure.

words.gloss_range: accusative construct quantifier governing the ship noun as exhaustive object scope
words.root_gloss_range: totality, encompassing, exhaustion, and encircling/crown imagery; locally universal quantification is selected

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the genitive complement completing the universal quantifier

words.prose: {{ar:كُلَّ}} ({{tr:kulla}}) converts the king’s taking into exhaustive policy by binding the following {{ar:سَفِينَةٍ}} ({{tr:safīnatin}}) as its genitive complement. The totalizing root can carry encircling pressure beside kingship, and its same-surah echoes at 18:45 and 18:54 invert here into coercive royal reach.

topics.headline: kulla makes the threat exhaustive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the king’s action is not against one ship but against the whole ship class.
topics.reason: The accusative construct quantifier depends on the following genitive ship noun and heads the exhaustive object.

topics.headline: totality carries encircling royal pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices royal power as an encircling, exhausting reach over the ship class, while the local sense remains universal quantification.
topics.reason: The crown/exhaustion root-family rows enrich the totality image but do not replace the quantifier function.

topics.headline: totality turns from divine scope to coercive reach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an inverted moral use of totality: comprehensive scope seen elsewhere in 18:45 and 18:54 is localized here to royal seizure.
topics.reason: The concrete references 18:45 and 18:54 support the contrast, while local grammar ties totality to ships.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive singular ship under the universal quantifier, naming any member of the vessel class
words.root_gloss_range: vessel/carrier field with supplied scraping and surface associations; locally a generic target vessel is selected
words.prose: {{ar:سَفِينَةٍ}} ({{tr:safīnatin}}) is no longer the known ship but any ship under the king’s policy, completing the move from particular case to class-wide threat. Variant adjectives for sound or intact ships expose the implicit selection criterion, while the rare ship lexeme frames the ayah’s logic: this vessel is protected because every serviceable vessel is at risk.

topics.headline: indefinite genitive names any target ship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the move from this one ship to any ship covered by the king’s rule.
topics.reason: The genitive indefinite singular completes the construct quantifier and distributes over the ship class.

topics.headline: variants expose serviceable-ship target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices why the defect works: variant adjectives make explicit that sound or intact ships are the desired targets, while the standard wording leaves that criterion compressed.
topics.reason: The accepted variant evidence clarifies the implicit selection criterion without overriding the standard zero-adjective form.

topics.headline: ship lexeme frames particular and class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the argument’s frame: the known ship is saved because every serviceable ship is threatened, with the same rare lexeme carrying the shift.
topics.reason: The rows connect the word to the opening ship, the final force word, rare distribution, and the definite-to-indefinite movement.

words.gloss_range: accusative indefinite verbal noun marking forcible wrongful seizure as manner and closure
words.root_gloss_range: wrongful taking by force, usurpation, seized property, and coercive appropriation; locally the legal-moral condemnation is selected
words.prose: {{ar:غَصْبًا}} ({{tr:ghaṣban}}) closes the ayah by naming the manner and moral category of the king’s action: forcible wrongful seizure. Its unique, final verbal-noun form turns broad taking into condemned usurpation, and its heavy closure answers the earlier protective defect with the coercive force that made protection necessary.

topics.headline: final accusative marks forced taking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the last word tells how the king takes: by coercive usurpation, not neutral acquisition.
topics.reason: The accusative verbal noun works as manner, with an intensifying absolute-object analysis also preserving coercive force.

topics.headline: ghaṣb names wrongful property violation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the vocabulary itself condemns the king’s taking as wrongful seizure of property.
topics.reason: The root-family evidence and local ownership context make this a legal-moral judgment, not merely a description of force.

topics.headline: unique final word seals the explanation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the explanation ends on the unique word for wrongful force, making coercion the last fact heard.
topics.reason: The row set supports hapax/form-level singularity and ayah-final position as a concentrated closing seal.

topics.headline: protective defect contrasts coercive usurpation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between two force words: controlled defect-making and heavy, final, wrongful seizure.
topics.reason: The sound and hapax convergence strengthens the contrast, while semantic judgment remains anchored in the manner word.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: فَأَرَدتُّ أَنْ أَعِيبَهَا ... يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًا
baseline_models.mechanism: A deliberately bounded defect changes the vessel's eligibility under a totalizing seizure rule: some integrity is surrendered so coercive possession bypasses the craft and leaves its owners the usable hull.

activation_trace.role: Surface scraping or removal supplies the material image for a controlled exterior impairment rather than destruction of the vessel.
The water-cutting craft is the productive asset whose continued navigability the intervention must preserve.
Intention makes the defect a selected means toward protection rather than accidental damage.
Sovereign power supplies the confiscatory regime against which the vessel is strategically disqualified.
Taking as physical possession names the threatened transfer that the defect is meant to interrupt.
Comprehensive inclusion makes an exception-producing blemish operationally necessary.
Unjust coercive seizure fixes the threat's legal direction and turns partial loss into resistance to dispossession.

changed_reading.before: The actor damages a sound boat because a nearby ruler threatens it.
changed_reading.after: The actor engineers a repairable exception to categorical confiscation, preserving the vessel through a measured partial loss.

baseline_models.mechanism: The owners are materially weak yet actively working; the vessel is therefore productive infrastructure, not a passive luxury. Preserving a usable hull preserves recurring labor, mobility, and earning capacity.

activation_trace.role: Poverty and social weakness identify owners exposed both to material loss and to stronger power.
Work-linked remuneration makes the vessel a means of livelihood rather than merely an owned object.
Manual workers supply the social body whose continuing agency depends on the craft.
Seafaring locates their work in repeated operation of a vessel, making navigability economically essential.
The ship that cleaves the water is the workers' mobile platform and retained means of production.

changed_reading.before: The boat is property belonging to poor people.
changed_reading.after: The boat is poor workers' livelihood platform, so preserving its usable core protects their capacity to work rather than wealth in the abstract.

context_deltas.mechanism: The enacted puncture and the observer's feared drowning establish two different damage thresholds. The later description as a blemish that saves the craft locates the intervention between them: conspicuous enough to defeat seizure, limited enough to leave the vessel recoverable.

activation_trace.role: The boarded water-cutting vessel identifies the same working craft before the intervention.
A slit or hole supplies the concrete act whose size and effect require calibration.
Drowning marks the feared destructive endpoint that the protective mechanism cannot actually reach.
Deliberate intent supplies the directional arrow from controlled breach to protective disqualification.
Coercive seizure supplies the alternative loss that makes a nonterminal breach rational.

structural_cues: 18:71 voices the projected result as drowning, whereas 18:79 retrospectively names the completed intervention only a defect.
The feminine object pronouns in خَرَقَهَا, أَخَرَقْتَهَا, and أَعِيبَهَا keep one vessel as the object across event, objection, and explanation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a puncture, a feared drowning, a later defect-label, and confiscation; I infer that the puncture was calibrated below destruction but above the ruler's acceptance threshold. A live alternative is that the boat remained unsafe until an unstated repair.

changed_reading.before: The puncture appears either reckless or simply destructive.
changed_reading.after: The puncture is a threshold intervention: enough visible damage to disqualify the boat, but not enough to erase its future use.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context makes incomplete knowledge and delayed disclosure part of the event's operation. The focus ayah does not merely append a motive to damage; it performs a temporal reclassification in which the hidden outcome turns an apparent wrong into asset preservation.

activation_trace.role: Complete cognitive enclosure names precisely what the immediate observer lacks when judging the damage.
Knowledge of an affair's interior distinguishes visible action from the concealed mechanism later disclosed.
Bringing something into view makes explanation a timed reveal rather than information available at the act.
Return to consequence or outcome makes the act intelligible from its eventual result.
Concealment behind what appears supplies the focus-side anchor for a threat and purpose unavailable to first sight.

structural_cues: 18:70 delays questioning until the guide himself produces a mention; 18:78 announces the interpretation; 18:79 then supplies the first explanation.
The causal وَكَانَ وَرَاءَهُم places the decisive threat outside the observer's immediately visible action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lack of encompassing knowledge, scheduled disclosure, outcome-oriented interpretation, and a concealed threat; I infer that delayed legibility is part of how the ayah asks the act to be read. The alternative is a narrower reading in which these cues govern only the dialogue, not the action's mechanism.

changed_reading.before: A later justification excuses an act that already has a stable visible meaning.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages an epistemic reversal: the act's moral and practical identity changes when its concealed future consequence becomes available.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same root frames two unlike takings: taking a person to account for a fault and taking a vessel into possession by force. Their proximity sharpens the focus threat as acquisition without adjudication, so the response alters the object's eligibility rather than appealing to the ruler's justice.

activation_trace.role: Taking-to-account for a fault supplies the nearby model of a taking tied to responsibility and possible excuse.
Taking into possession supplies the ruler's materially acquisitive action.
Force and injustice block an accountability reading and expose the taking as dispossession.

structural_cues: 18:73 joins تُؤَاخِذْنِى to a specified fault, while 18:79 joins يَأْخُذُ to totalized ships and غَصْبًا.
The focus ayah offers no hearing, fault, or exception procedure; it creates an exception materially.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two local uses of the same root and explicitly labels the second coercive; I infer a contrast between adjudicative and acquisitive taking. The alternative is ordinary polysemy without deliberate cross-activation.

changed_reading.before: The king's taking is a generic external danger.
changed_reading.after: The king's taking is anti-adjudicative capture, so a physical exception is used where moral appeal or due process has no purchase.

context_deltas.mechanism: The ship and wall episodes become opposite surface operations with one custodial logic. A sound-looking vessel is impaired so predatory power will not take it; a failing wall is made upright so concealed wealth will not become accessible before its vulnerable owners can claim it.

activation_trace.role: The raised wall supplies a visible barrier whose condition regulates access to what lies behind or beneath it.
Dissolution of built structure supplies the impending exposure that must be prevented.
Making the wall stand provides the inverse material operation to blemishing the vessel.
Children cut off from a guardian supply vulnerable owners parallel to the materially weak boat workers.
Stored wealth supplies the asset whose access is delayed by maintaining its cover.
Material weakness supplies the focus beneficiaries who likewise cannot withstand premature exposure to stronger actors.
Covering or placing behind appearance links altered surfaces to controlled visibility and access.

structural_cues: Both explanations use أَمَّا ... فَكَانَ لِـ to identify an asset and vulnerable beneficiaries before stating an intention.
18:82 explicitly keeps the treasure under the wall until the owners reach maturity and extract it; 18:79 keeps the vessel with its workers by making it unattractive to seizure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opposite repairs, vulnerable owners, concealed or threatened assets, and delayed safe access; I infer a common custody rule that changes surfaces to regulate stronger outsiders' access. A live alternative is that the two episodes share compassion but not one material strategy.

changed_reading.before: Blemishing the boat is an isolated exception justified by one ruler.
changed_reading.after: Blemishing is one polarity of protective custody: a surface may be degraded or reinforced according to which state best controls premature access to a vulnerable person's asset.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence distinguishes operative intention from ultimate authorization. The focus speaker can truthfully say 'I intended' at the level of chosen means while the closing disclosure places that action inside a higher intention and denies autonomous command.

activation_trace.role: Singular willing anchors the actor's proximate selection of the boat-defecting means.
Plural willing expands the agency register across the explanations instead of leaving every act at one grammatical level.
The Lord's willing supplies the encompassing purposive source into which the actor's practical intention is nested.
Lordship and sovereignty identify the superior level of authorization rather than another local preference.
The actor's concrete doing remains affirmed even while its independent authorship is denied.
Command as binding direction supplies the authority under which the action is performed.

structural_cues: The explanations move from فَأَرَدتُّ in 18:79 to فَأَرَدْنَا in 18:81 and فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ in 18:82.
The closing وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَمْرِى preserves first-person action while explicitly denying action from independent command.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies singular, plural, and divine willing plus a denial of independent command; I infer nested agency in which local choice executes authorized purpose. The alternative is that the pronoun shifts distinguish only the three acts and should not be systematized beyond them.

changed_reading.before: فَأَرَدتُّ presents a private calculation by an autonomous actor.
changed_reading.after: فَأَرَدتُّ names proximate practical intention inside commissioned agency: the actor chooses the means without claiming ultimate authorship.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it reads the defect as information control through form-distant surface and concealment branches, not merely as loss of value. It remains anchored to deliberate blemishing of the vessel before a power located beyond immediate view. Downstream prose should present it as a possible camouflage mechanism, not as a lexical translation of أَعِيبَهَا.

activation_trace.role: Changing or stripping a surface activates the exterior as the intervention's informational layer.
Exposure in open space makes visible condition consequential to an inspecting power.
Concealing a thing by presenting something else supplies the camouflage function assigned to the visible defect.
Possessive taking supplies the inspection outcome that altered appearance is meant to avert.

changed_reading.before: The blemish only lowers the vessel's material value.
changed_reading.after: The blemish may act as surface camouflage, hiding a still-serviceable productive core behind the appearance of seizure-unworthiness.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates the ship-stabilizer sense of س ك ن from the noun مَسَاكِين rather than translating the noun by it. The co-presence of poor owners and their vessel keeps the activation focus-anchored and makes their social stability depend materially on the craft. Downstream prose should mark this as wordplay-like resonance, not historical derivation or primary semantics.

activation_trace.role: The apparatus that steadies a ship activates the craft as what materially stabilizes the owners' precarious lives.
Poverty and weakness keep the stabilizer image attached to the named beneficiaries rather than to nautical mechanics alone.
The actual vessel supplies the concrete object through which the distant stabilizing branch becomes functionally coherent.
Work-derived livelihood turns nautical stability into continuing household and economic stability.

changed_reading.before: The poor happen to own and operate a boat.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the boat is their external stabilizing organ: damaging it just enough to retain it protects the very means by which precarious workers remain socially and economically steady.

strongest_changes: The puncture is bounded between visible disqualification and the explicitly feared endpoint of drowning.
Delayed disclosure does not merely excuse the act; it reclassifies the act through its concealed outcome.
The wall parallel reveals a general custody mechanism in which opposite surface changes regulate access to vulnerable owners' assets.
The closing agency sequence nests the speaker's practical intention within a higher command without erasing his concrete action.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah concentrates material engineering, labor protection, coercive law, controlled visibility, delayed knowledge, and layered agency into one small defect. Context most strongly changed the reading by showing that the defect's size, moral identity, and authorship are all relational rather than visible in the puncture alone.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not state the exact defect, its repair cost, or how reliably it exempted the vessel from seizure.
The accountability/confiscation contrast may be local root polysemy rather than an intended cross-episode opposition.
The camouflage and ship-stabilizer activations are deliberately exploratory and should not displace the stronger material and custodial models.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Intentional damage preserves intentional work.** `ع م ل` B001 (“intentional doing and work”) belongs to the poor sailors, while the teacher’s intended defect blocks the king’s seizure. The garden owner assumed intact form meant durable good (18:35), and the barrier later remains good only temporarily (18:98). I infer that controlled impairment can preserve a livelihood by changing how predatory power classifies an object. The flaw is functional shielding, not negation of value.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:98 showed the broader pattern in which deliberate material impairment or removal can preserve a bounded good.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **A defect preserves the vessel by changing its classification.** `ع ي ب/B001` is a blemish or made defect; dormant `ع ي ب/B002` is a repository for goods or secrets, and `B003` is water breaching a bank. A working vessel is a carrying repository exposed to water, while the king takes every qualifying ship; the puncture lowers it below that seizure rule. The packet states intention and threat, while I infer the classification arrow. `أَعِيبَهَا` reads as targeted value reduction that preserves the owners’ productive container.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:80–82 repeated hidden causal arcs and ended with `وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَمْرِي`, clarifying that tactical defect was authorized rather than private cleverness.

concept_map.definition: Temel anlam, su üzerinde yol alan gemidir; adı su yüzünü yarıp açmasıyla açıklanır. Bundan gemiyi kullanan kişi adı ve benzetmeyle rahat binilen her taşıt anlamı türemiştir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه راودته على كذا، أي أردته على فعله، والمراودة التي يكون فيها منازعة إرادة غيرك وصرفه عن رأيه.
يدخل فيه راد الكلأ وارتاده بمعنى طلبه، والرائد المرسل أو الطالب للكلإ، والرجل الرأد بمعنى الرائد.
يدخل فيه راد الشيء إذا جاء وذهب، ورياد الإبل واختلافها في المرعى، والمراد موضع التردد، ورادت المرأة إلى بيوت جاراتها، وراد وساده إذا لم يستقر.
يدخل فيه أرود في السير إذا رفق، والمشي على رود، ورويد ورويدك بمعنى مهلا وأمهل، والرادة من الرياح السهلة التي لا تهب بشدة.
يدخل فيه الرائد بمعنى يد الرحى أو العود الذي تدار به، والمرود بمعنى الميل والحديدة التي تدور في اللجام ومحور البكرة من حديد.
يدخل فيه رائد العين، أي عوارها الذي يرود فيها.
يدخل فيه جارية رود بمعنى شابة، ومعها الرؤدة والرأدة بالهمز في الصحاح بمعنى الشابة الحسنة.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın tam çekirdeğini verir: alınan bir şey, bundan yoksun bırakılan sahibi, haksızlık ve zor kullanımı birlikte belirtilir.

error_profile.preserves: Alma eylemini, sahibinden yoksun bırakmayı, haksızlığı ve zor kullanımını eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Haksızlığın bağlamdan açıkça anlaşıldığı ve sahibin elinden alınma ilişkisinin öne çıktığı anlatımlarda doğal bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Bir şeyin sahibinden zor kullanılarak alınmasını doğal bir anlatımla korur.
error_profile.loses: Haksızlık koşulunu sözün içinde açıkça belirtmez ve bu koşulu bağlama bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Alınan şeyin mal olduğu bağlamlarda, zorlayıcı sahiplik müdahalesini öne çıkaran doğal bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Sahibin malından zor kullanılarak yoksun bırakılması yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Dalın mal dışındaki şeylere de uygulanabilen daha geniş nesne kapsamını daraltır.
error_profile.collision: El koyma sözü bazı bağlamlarda yetkili ve hukuka uygun bir işlemi de çağrıştırabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Tek bir şeyin sahibinden haksız ve zorla alınmasını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Malın tümünü alma ve savaş bağlamındaki yağma kapsamını özellikle taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her ikisi de malın sahibinin elinden alınması alanında buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal, herhangi bir şeyin sahibinden haksız ve zorla alınmasına dayanır; komşu dal ise malın tümünün alınması, yağma ve savaşla bağlantılı mahrum bırakma görünümünü öne çıkarır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Zorlamanın sonucu olarak bir şeyin sahibinden alınmasını zorunlu tutar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir kişiyi, ortada alınan bir şey bulunmadan da istemediği bir davranışa zorlamayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da bir kişinin direncini güç kullanarak aşma yönü bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalda güç, bir şeyi sahibinden almak için kullanılır; komşu dalda ise çekirdek, kişinin iradesini bastırıp onu bir davranışa zorlamaktır ve nesne aktarımı gerekmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bir şeyin sahibinden haksız biçimde alınmasını kurucu koşul olarak taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Sertçe yakalama, vurma veya öfkeyle öldürme gibi alma dışındaki şiddet eylemlerine uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her ikisi de güç ve şiddet kullanılarak gerçekleştirilen alma görünümünü içerebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalda şiddet, sahibini bir şeyden haksız yere yoksun bırakan almanın aracıdır; komşu dal ise sert saldırıyı ve yakalamayı öne çıkarır, haksız edinmeyi zorunlu kılmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sahibinden yoksun bırakmayı haksızlık ve zor kullanımıyla birlikte gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir şeye önce davranmayı, onu elde etmeyi veya üzerinde ısrarlı bir sahiplik iddiasında bulunmayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: öne davranıp alma ve sahiplik iddiası
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da bir şeyi elde etme ve ona sahip çıkma çevresinde kesişir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın sınırını haksız ve zorlayıcı mahrum bırakma çizer; komşu dalda ise önce davranma ya da iddia etme yeterli olabilir, zor kullanımı ve haksızlık kurucu değildir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bir şeyi mevcut sahibinden haksız yere zorla alma eylemini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: İnsanları zorla bağımlı kılma ve onlar üzerinde sahiplik kurma durumunu anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da güç yoluyla başkası üzerinde haksız denetim kurma görünümü vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın nesnesi sahibinden alınan bir şeydir ve çekirdek bir alma olayıdır; komşu dal insanları bağımlılaştırıp onlar üzerinde sürekli sahiplik veya egemenlik kurmaya yönelir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Sekiz komşu adayın tamamı değerlendirildi. Zorla alma, genel zorlama, yağma, sert saldırı, sahiplik iddiası ve insanları zorla bağımlı kılma sınırı aydınlatan beş karşılaştırmada işlendi; yalnızca karşılaşınca elde etme, hakkı eksiltme ve genel zarar verme adayları yeterli çekirdek örtüşmesi sağlamadığı için yayımlanmadı.
